# Didache Chapter 10 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 10 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/DID_010_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 10

**1** After you have been satisfied, give thanks in this way:

**2** We give you thanks, holy Father, for your holy name which you have caused to dwell in our hearts, and for the knowledge and faith and immortality which you made known to us through Jesus your servant. To you be glory forever.

**3** You, Lord Almighty, created all things for the sake of your name; you gave food and drink to human beings to enjoy, so that they might give you thanks. And to us you have graciously granted spiritual food and spiritual drink and eternal life, through Jesus your servant.

**4** Above all, we thank you because you are mighty. To you be glory forever.

**5** Remember, Lord, your Church — to rescue it from all evil and to make it perfect in your love, and gather it together, now sanctified, from the four winds into your kingdom which you have prepared for it. For yours is the power and the glory forever.

**6** Let grace come, and let this world pass away. Hosanna to the God of David. If any are holy, let them come; if any are not, let them repent. Maranatha! [Our Lord, come!] Amen.

**7** Allow the prophets to give thanks as they will.

---

*LOGOS notes: Ch. 10 is the post-communion thanksgiving, one of the richest liturgical texts of the early church. V.2 — God's name "dwelling" in the hearts of the community is tabernacle language. V.3 — the contrast between ordinary food (given to all humanity) and "spiritual food and drink" (given to the community) articulates the eucharist as a special gift within a larger theology of creation and provision. V.5 — "four winds" (τεσσάρων ἀνέμων) = the four corners of the earth (cf. Matt 24:31; Mk 13:27). V.6 — "Hosanna to the God of David" is a remarkable combination: Hosanna (הוֹשַׁע נָא = "save now!") addressed not to the Son of David but to the God of David. The invitation "if any are holy, let them come" may be a liturgical call to communion. Maranatha — the Aramaic prayer preserved intact (cf. 1 Cor 16:22; Rev 22:20).*
